data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) as a non-probabilistic metric to justify preferring corroborated theories, but this fails Popper's own terms because Popper later conceded that verisimilitude cannot be formally defined for false theories without collapsing into probabilistic measures. Since all scientific theories are technically false (having been falsified or being falsifiable), the claim that one false theory is 'closer to truth' than another lacks the rigorous logical footing Popper demands, effectively smuggling in an inductive assumption that past survival indicates future proximity to truth.
